dēcarmĭno , avi, 1, v. a. de-carmen,
I.to make prose of verse, to disarrange the order of the words in a verse: “sed hic ordo nobis verborum faciendus est, ut versus hujus decarminata contextio ipsa se magis exponere videatur,” Cassiod. in Psa. 130, 3, 4 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
